content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Image Analysis:**

- **Plant part affected**: Stem — shown as a longitudinal (lengthwise) cross-section cut to reveal internal tissue
- **Key visual features**:
  - The stem interior shows extensive **dark brown to black discoloration** running the length of the vascular/pith tissue
  - The outer cortex remains green and relatively intact
  - There is a surface canker/dark lesion visible on the left side of the stem exterior
  - The discoloration is concentrated in the central vascular and pith region
  - No obvious white mycelium or sclerotia (which would suggest Sclerotinia)

**Reasoning:**

The image shows the classic diagnostic presentation of **Verticillium Wilt**: a stem cut longitudinally to reveal brown-to-black discoloration of the vascular tissue. This is the standard field/lab diagnostic method — cutting the stem and observing the characteristic dark vascular streaking. The cortex remaining green while the internal vascular tissue is darkened is the hallmark feature of Verticillium dahliae infection.

- **Bacterial Wilt** would typically show bacterial ooze/streaming when cut
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** would show white cottony mycelium and hard black sclerotia in the pith
- **Bacterial Canker** shows similar vascular browning but with more pith involvement and pith discoloration typically lighter (tan/brown rather than near-black)
- The pattern here — dark central vascular discoloration with intact outer cortex — is most consistent with Verticillium Wilt
